# Signal Weekly — Oct 5–Oct 12, 2026

*Oct 5–Oct 12, 2026*

A roundup of what came through the dashboard this week, across 4 categories.

## Tech news

- **[How Apple Puts Indigenous Languages on the iPhone Keyboard](https://www.wired.com/story/how-apple-puts-indigenous-languages-on-the-iphone-keyboard/)** (Wired) — To save endangered languages, tech companies like Apple are working with Indigenous communities to meet the next generation where they type.
- **[Feds Got Warrants to Use Fake Cell Towers to Hunt Down Don Lemon’s Producer](https://www.wired.com/story/feds-got-warrants-to-use-fake-cell-towers-to-hunt-down-don-lemons-producer/)** (Wired) — Investigators also sought permission to use an invasive surveillance tool called a cell-site simulators against journalist Georgia Fort and a Minnesota state Senate candidate.
- **[AlterMe Review: Fitness Built Around My DNA](https://www.wired.com/review/alterme-fitness-and-wellness-program/)** (Wired) — Six months with AlterMe’s smart ring and a fitness app helped me build better habits, but the genetic insights were less revealing than I’d hoped.
- **[A New Anti-Aging Drug Looks to Turn Back the Clock on Skin Age](https://www.wired.com/story/new-anti-aging-drug-trial-for-skin/)** (Wired) — After four weeks of using the cream, participants lowered the biological age of their skin by about two years on average.
- **[Far-Right Election Groups Are Now Targeting Nursing Homes](https://www.wired.com/story/republican-election-groups-are-now-targeting-nursing-homes/)** (Wired) — Inspired by new guidance from the Trump administration, right-wing election groups are targeting nursing homes, baselessly claiming that left-wing groups are stealing residents’ votes.
- **[One killed after Riyadh airport hit again, a day after deadly strike killed 13](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxOa2ZUXzc2NDROUjFFVXpwbFA1S0hXSEZ0eGlYMkdNNDQtay13MDkzc3VBZUdQZ3FDREtlelF1Ri1tbEl0eXF0ZkxsbUZkaG13T1V0RHlFWXBmZ0pFa3JsRHhUVGZJbUd4cWJnaFRsMzh6TEowM0ZQOGo4anM5MjBvcld4bU1kWlAz?oc=5)** (CBS News) —

Concept-based attribution methods interpret models using human-understandable concepts. Existing concept-based methods can only interpret classification and regression models. - **[AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities](http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13928v1)** (Andis Draguns, Sumeet Ramesh Motwani et al.) — Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. ## Reviews

- **[How is Microsoft's Magnetic Connect different from Apple's MagSafe for MacBooks?](https://www.engadget.com/2281340/how-microsoft-magnetic-connect-different-from-apple-macbook-magsafe/)** (Engadget Reviews) — Magnetic Connect and MagSafe for MacBooks have a lot in common, but the Magnetic Connect charger brings more versatility.
- **[8BitDo Ultimate 2 review: The best Switch 2 controller out there](https://www.engadget.com/2282781/8bitdo-ultimate-2-review/)** (Engadget Reviews) — Everything is within reach on 8BitDo's Ultimate 2, even for small hands.
- **[WhatsApp users may soon be able to schedule messages](https://www.engadget.com/2283518/whatsapp-users-may-soon-be-able-to-schedule-messages/)** (Engadget Reviews) — WhatsApp is finally allowing message scheduling, a feature that's been available on Telegram since 2019.
- **[Microsoft's president says AI is less regulated than a carton of milk](https://www.engadget.com/2283487/microsoft-president-ai-less-regulated-than-a-carton-of-milk/)** (Engadget Reviews) — Milk can't hack companies and governments like AI definitely can, but it's still subject to more regulation.
